freedom of speech is an axiom. there should be no attempt to restrain it or restrict it on any grounds, that includes hate speech, racism, political correctness etc. because all of these restrictions are subjective. for example if I say "kill the muslims" then that is counted as hate speech. well in that case large parts of the koran is also hate speech because it talks of killing the kafirs and raping the kafirs and so on. and any practising muslim is by default guilty of hate speech.

so ... completely unrestricted. because the smallest restriction is going to pervert the whole thing. the thing about the one bad apple applies here.

but unbridled free speech is merely an enabler. it is not the objective. using free speech as the base, we can then talk through any and all issues, and develop arguments and move to a logical conclusion on any moral question. any question at all. and because we just talk about freedom of speech as the end goal, we are unable to move past.

we need to learn and teach critical thinking, how to argue, how to present views, how to avoid fallacies... we need to build arguments to support positions, and we need to read counter arguments and either point out flaws in them or accept them. if we follow that process we will make progress. if the process by which we conclude on something is made transparent, then anyone can come in later and see the process, the logical procession. and if they find any flaw with it, then they can point it out and we can open that debate again.

so what we really need is three things:

  1. a showcase/curated list of arguments and counter arguments that conclude on something. i want to say "frequently argued positions" or faps.

  2. free information on critical thinking, making arguments, fallacies etc.

  3. sandbox forums where arguments can be practiced and help can be sought on how to improve arguments so that they reach a proper quality.

so we have to move beyond simply talking about freedom of speech and start at the next level. where we will quickly start concluding on moral and ethical points.

I bought the Star Wars Humble Bundle and wanted to play KOTOR but the game crashed right after the character customization screen. I have Windows 7 64 bit and an AMD graphics card. I tried different fixes and this is the one that worked for me:

  1. Go to the kotor installation folder (C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\SteamApps\common\swkotor)

  2. Open swconfig.exe

  3. Change the resolution to your native resolution or the highest resolution available, uncheck ’V-Sync’, uncheck ‘Enable Hardware Mouse’, check ‘Disable Movies’

 

Here are some other fixes that might work

  • Run in compatibility mode - find the swkotor.exe file in the kotor folder, right click it, select ’properties’, then 'compatibility' tab - set it to run in compatibility mode for Windows XP SP2 and check the box 'run this program as an administrator'.

  • Disable Steam overlay - open Steam, go to ’library’, right click on kotor, select ’properties’, uncheck ’enable the Steam overlay while in-game’.

  • Disable frame buffer and soft shadow in the games options menu.

  • Manually changing the values in the .ini file in the kotor folder from Fullscreen=1 to Fullscreen=0 did NOT work for me.
